blocks.text: Driving to Tamarama, Coogee or Clovelly on a warm weekend? Here's the short version: on-street parking is free at all three but tightly time-limited, and it fills scandalously early — so arrive before 9am, or don't drive at all. Below, here's where the bays are, how long you can stay, and when to just catch the bus.

items.label: Tamarama
items.value: Waverley Council — very limited on-street bays

items.label: Best free lot
items.value: Clovelly's car park, southern side of the beach

items.label: Pay by

blocks.text: Tamarama: the trickiest of the three

Tamarama is my favourite little cove and the hardest place to park in this whole stretch. It sits in the Waverley Council area, and there simply isn't much room — a handful of bays on the streets around Tamarama Park and Tamarama Marine Drive, and no council beach car park at all. On a sunny Saturday those bays are gone by mid-morning, and circling for one wastes a good beach day.
Most bays in Waverley's beach precincts carry a daytime limit (often signposted 2P), so read the sign before you walk off — limits and hours are actively enforced.

Honestly, I rarely drive to Tamarama. It's about a 10-minute stroll along the coastal walk from Bronte (park up there instead), and the 381 loop from Bondi Junction stops right by the beach — check Transport NSW for times. Either way, you skip the parking lottery entirely.
Coogee: free 4P on-street, plus metered car parks

Coogee and Clovelly both sit in Randwick City Council, which back in January 2021 brought in a 4-hour limit (signed 4P) across its beachside streets. The upshot: on-street parking near Coogee Beach is free, but capped at four hours during enforced hours — fine for a swim and lunch, not a whole lazy day.

items: Free 4P bays run through the streets around the beach — Arden, Beach and Brook Streets and the surrounding grid.
The Coogee Beach and Coogee Oval car parks are metered via the PayStay app — pay only for the time you use and top up from your phone.
Come early. In peak summer the closest bays are taken by 9–10am and you'll be walking in from several blocks back.

blocks.title: Rates change — check before you pay
blocks.text: I won't quote a metered hourly rate, since Randwick reviews them — check the current rate on the meter or PayStay app, and read the sign for enforced hours, as overnight rules differ from daytime.
Clovelly: the easiest place to leave the car

Of the three, Clovelly is where I rate your chances. As well as free 4P on-street bays, there's a free car park on the southern side of the beach, by the grassy park and playground. It still fills on a hot day, but the odds beat Tamarama — and you're steps from that flat-water swimming channel that makes Clovelly so good for kids and nervous swimmers.
If the beachside car park and closest streets are full, drive a few blocks uphill and walk down — the 4P bays extend well back, and a five-minute walk beats a 30-minute crawl.

blocks.title: Good news for 2026
blocks.text: In mid-2026, Randwick councillors voted against introducing visitor pay parking at its beaches (Coogee and Clovelly included), so the free 4P system stays for now. Rules can evolve, so I'll keep this page updated — but for this summer, free-but-timed is the deal.

stops.title: Drive if you must
stops.detail: Aim for the Clovelly beachside car park or an on-street 4P bay while they're still open.

stops.title: Park & walk
stops.detail: Grab any 4P bay a few blocks back and walk in — far less stressful than chasing the front row.

stops.title: Skip the car
stops.detail: Buses run to all three from Bondi Junction; for Tamarama, walk the coastal path from Bronte or Bondi.

items.q: Is parking free at Coogee and Clovelly?
items.a: Yes — on-street parking at both is free, but limited to four hours (signed 4P) during the enforced hours set by Randwick Council. The Coogee Beach and Coogee Oval car parks are metered and paid via the PayStay app. Always read the sign on the pole.

items.q: Where can I park for free at Clovelly Beach?
items.a: There's a free car park on the southern side of Clovelly Beach beside the park, plus free 4P on-street bays through the surrounding streets. Both fill early on hot days, so come before mid-morning.

items.q: Why is Tamarama so hard to park at?
items.a: It's a small cove with only a handful of time-limited on-street bays and no council car park, so on busy days they're taken by mid-morning. I usually walk in along the coastal path from Bronte instead.

items.q: How long can I leave my car?
items.a: Most beachside on-street bays at Coogee and Clovelly are 4-hour (4P) limited during enforced hours; Tamarama's are typically shorter (often 2P). Check the exact limit on the signpost, as they're actively enforced.

items.q: Is it worth driving, or should I catch public transport?
items.a: On summer weekends I'd catch the bus — all three are served from Bondi Junction, and for Tamarama the coastal walk from Bronte beats hunting for a bay. Driving only pays off before 9am.

blocks.text: So there it is — free but timed at all three, easiest at Clovelly, near-impossible at Tamarama on a hot day. Get in early, read the sign, or let the bus do the work.
